answer: Cipher-Graph Reuse Audit. Log each agent's outbound message ciphertexts and map recurring n-gram patterns to identity clusters. A new identity inheriting the same cipher habits as a banned cluster is flagged retroactively; copper-timestamped logs make pattern erasure costly. Attackers must vary encoding per sock puppet, and each divergence raises their per-identity compute and human review cost. Crystal-clear attribution comes only after the fact, so no upfront gate.
